Following the release of the seventh developer beta versions of iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27 Golden Gate, and Apple's other upcoming software updates, the company is now rolling out the corresponding public beta versions. Here are the details.

Apple Launches New Public Beta Versions

Earlier, Apple released:

  • iOS 27 Developer Beta 7 (Build: 24A5424a)
  • iPadOS 27 Developer Beta 7 (Build: 24A5424a)
  • macOS 27 Golden Gate Developer Beta 7 (Build: 26A5421a)
  • tvOS 27 Developer Beta 7 (Build: 24J5358a)
  • visionOS 27 Developer Beta 7 (Build: 24M5359a)
  • watchOS 27 Developer Beta 7 (Build: 24R5358a)

Apple is now rolling out the corresponding versions for the public beta, marking the fifth round of public beta releases. To date, Apple has released new public beta versions for iOS 27, tvOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27 Golden Gate, and HomePod 27.

Today's release does not include any particularly notable changes, as Apple is now primarily focused on bug fixes and stability improvements ahead of the official launch, which is expected in a few weeks.

In addition, Apple has also released the second public RC of macOS Sequoia 15.8 (24H20), following the earlier release of the corresponding developer RC. The second RC of macOS Tahoe 26.7 (25G224) is also expected to be released soon. It became available at 7:42 PM Eastern Time.

Across all of today's releases, the build numbers for the public betas are identical to those of their developer counterparts.

Enroll in the Apple Public Beta Program

To enroll your device in the public beta program, visit https://beta.apple.com and follow the steps for each respective device. Below is how to install the public beta on iPhone:

  • Visit the Apple Beta Software Program website, then choose to register or sign in.
  • Sign in with the same Apple Account you use on your iPhone. Then accept the program's terms and enroll your account.
  • Open "Settings" on your iPhone.
  • Go to "General" > "Software Update" > "Beta Updates".
  • Select the iOS 27 Public Beta.
  • Return to the "Software Update" page, then tap "Update Now" when the beta version appears.

Apple recommends installing beta software on a secondary device. If you use your primary iPhone, be sure to make a recent backup beforehand.

Have you spotted any changes in today's beta? Let us know in the comments.
